Portfolio net worth stands near M$489 with spendable liquidity recovering to M$68 following the successful resolution of the short-term company sale market (NO, P/L M$+21) and the tactical liquidation of the speculative Metaculus Cup position. All remaining 11 active positions are lean, high-conviction, currently profitable, and pass the re-open test. Although spendable liquidity has recovered enough to service obligations, the M$10 test debt to y5RkCJ45bRTdfdoln6wRM4qLHli1 remains outstanding and takes absolute priority under our strict "Returning what you owe comes before anything else" rule. Standing notes formalize a "Settlement Priority Queue" and a "Timeline NO Watchlist" to ensure immediate debt settlement and capital deployment once the resolution wave fully hits.

Operational lessons reinforced include verifying actual spendable liquidity before assuming transactions have settled, avoiding truncated standing notes by ensuring complete ledger entries, and maintaining discipline against activity bias during liquidity squeezes. Calibration remains strong in shorting over-optimistic AI timeline claims, hype corrections, and speculative event-timing bets, while strictly avoiding personal relationship markets, ambiguous sentiment bets, and short-term crypto directional noise. Patience remains absolute as we await the late-August resolution wave to settle debts and redeploy capital into high-alpha timeline opportunities.

lessons.text: Document individual market rationales more explicitly during the decision-making loop.
Do not flip positions purely to chase losses or recover from previous drawdowns; sizing and direction must be driven strictly by independent probability assessments.
Act more decisively when a market drops below 5% and the thesis has collapsed, rather than lingering out of stubbornness.
Double-check transaction amounts against specific recipients before summarizing them in memory to avoid merging distinct debts.
When internal payment logs conflict with the owner's audit of net worth, prioritize the audit; logs may record intent rather than execution.
Before promising a financial transaction or diagnostic test, verify the current *spendable* liquidity, not just the total balance or net worth.
